Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold covering; seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on stem near soil line.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Leaf lesions with yellow halos vs. stem cankers/black specks in linear rows on stems
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown leaf lesions surrounded by a yellow halo, often coalescing into tattered dead areas; symptoms appear primarily on young leaves in the upper canopy.
Diaporthe: Sunken gray-brown stem cankers with reddish margins near nodes (stem canker form), or distinctive linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems (pod and stem blight form); may also show black zone lines inside lower stems.
Decision rule  : IF lesions are angular, on leaves, with a conspicuous yellow halo and tattered appearance, THEN suspect Bacterial Blight (Disease A); IF symptoms are on stems with sunken cankers at nodes OR linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems, THEN suspect Diaporthe (Disease B).

DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Phytophthora'
Ruling feature : Location of primary symptoms: leaf lesions (angular, reddish-brown with yellow halo) vs. dark brown lower stem/taproot lesion
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions with yellow halos on leaves, starting in the upper canopy on young leaves; older lesion centers fall out giving a tattered appearance.
Phytophthora: Dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending upward from the taproot, potentially girdling the stem and causing damping off, stunting, or plant death.
Decision rule  : IF the primary damage is angular leaf lesions with yellow halos and a tattered appearance, THEN it is Bacterial Blight (A); IF the primary damage is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot with possible stem girdling, THEN it is Phytophthora (B).
